chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abī Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:
I asked him, saying: How should I act when I become junub? He said: Wash your hand and your private part, perform wudu (ablution) as for salat (prayer), then perform ghusl (ritual bath).
Thus, the correct way regarding this report is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation, and that does not conflict with that.

key_terms.أَجْنَبْتُ: I entered the state of janabah, requiring ritual purification
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: the ritual ablution done for salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is wudu (ablution) required before ghusl for janabah according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the procedure for one in a state of janabah, mentioning washing the hand and private part, performing wudu (ablution), and then performing ghusl (ritual bath). The closing statement clarifies that the instruction for wudu before ghusl is to be understood as recommended rather than obligatory.
